issues.title: support prague / l4s congestion response
issues.author: kazuho
issues.body:
ABBA currently assumes that each congestion event reduces the congestion window by a fixed multiplicative factor beta. The same machinery can be applied to Prague/L4S with relatively little change.

When queue buildup is not visible, ABBA accelerates the increase once:

```c
cwnd > cwnd_prior * (2 - beta)
```

Prague reduces the congestion window on CE feedback using approximately:

```c
beta = 1 - alpha / 2
```

where alpha is Prague's EWMA estimate of the CE-marked fraction.

By simply recording the effective beta used for each congestion-window reduction, ABBA can use that recorded value for the following congestion epoch. The existing ABBA rules, including the acceleration threshold above, can then be applied unchanged.

Prague uses a CUBIC arm on a per-period basis, as in Apple's implementation. That arm can use the existing ABBA behavior unchanged.

Prague's existing adaptation of alpha can also remain unchanged. If ABBA accelerates too aggressively and causes a higher CE-marking fraction, Prague will naturally increase alpha, resulting in a stronger subsequent reduction. Therefore, no ABBA-specific adjustment of alpha appears necessary.
